items.stem: A user needs read-only access to a shared folder. Share permission is Full Control but NTFS is Read. What is the effective access?

options.text: Read, because the most restrictive of the combined permissions applies
options.rationale: Correct: NTFS and share permissions combine to the most restrictive result.

options.text: Full Control, because the share permission wins
options.rationale: Share permissions do not override more restrictive NTFS permissions.
Read is granted by both layers at minimum, so access is not denied.

options.text: Modify, as a compromise between the two
options.rationale: Effective access is the most restrictive, not an average.

items.explanation: Correct: the effective permission is the most restrictive of NTFS and share.

items.stem: Which TWO are good reasons to use PowerShell over manual clicking for administration? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Tasks can be scripted and repeated consistently
options.rationale: Correct: scripting gives repeatable, auditable results.

options.text: Changes can be applied to many machines at once
options.rationale: Correct: PowerShell scales a task across many hosts.

options.text: It removes the need to understand permissions
options.rationale: Permissions still apply regardless of the tool used.
PowerShell runs under the same security model, not around it.

items.explanation: Correct: PowerShell gives repeatable scripting and scale across machines.

items.stem: A Windows machine fails to boot normally after a driver update. Which recovery step is most appropriate first?

options.text: Boot into Safe Mode and roll back the driver
options.rationale: Correct: Safe Mode loads minimal drivers so the bad driver can be removed.
Reinstalling is excessive before trying targeted recovery.
A software driver fault does not require hardware replacement.
This does not address a driver fault and risks data loss.

items.explanation: Correct: Safe Mode lets you roll back the offending driver.
